terms.meaning: a library that builds web pages out of reusable pieces called components.
a reusable piece of a page, such as a button or a panel, that shows content and can react to user actions.
a request to the server whose result is stored and shown, and refreshed when needed.
a quick server check that counts how many projects a chosen scope would include before a full run starts.
the method the server used to build a run. Two engines are named here: recipe-v3 and legacy.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and page setup
sections.what: Brings in the libraries, shared parts and helper files that the page needs. It does not show anything on screen by itself.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Shared pieces are imported so the same header, scope picker and data functions are reused across tools.
sections.watch_out: If one of these imported files is moved or renamed, the whole page will fail to load.

sections.name: RunSwitch
sections.title: Choosing the right run view
sections.what: While a run loads, shows a spinner. Once loaded, shows the recipe-v3 view for newer runs and the older lessons view for all other runs. It also keeps checking the run every 2 seconds until the run reaches a final status.
sections.why: Different engines produce different kinds of results, so each needs its own display. Reason for the 2 second check is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The final status list in llApi decides when checking stops. A status missing from that list makes the page keep checking forever.

sections.name: DemoReplay
sections.title: Replaying the recorded demo
sections.what: Loads the built-in recorded run for the demo and shows it in the recipe view in replay mode. If the recording cannot load, it shows a red error message with the reason.
sections.why: Lets a visitor see a complete example without starting a real run, which costs time and resources.
sections.watch_out: The demo depends on a recording on the server. If that recording is removed, this view shows only the error.

sections.name: LessonsLearntPage (part 1)
sections.title: Page state, scope and precheck
sections.what: Reads the web address to decide between the start screen, a saved run, the demo and replay. It keeps the chosen scope, loads a precheck count when the scope is not empty, and prepares the industry totals the summary needs.
sections.why: The precheck lets users see how many projects they would get before they spend a run. The web address controls the page so links can be shared and reopened.
sections.watch_out: The precheck is only requested when the scope is not empty and no run is open, so changes to those conditions change which requests happen.

sections.name: LessonsLearntPage (part 2)
sections.title: Summary panel and start button
sections.what: Shows the project total, a bar for each industry with its share, and a start button labelled Build lessons deck. The button stays off when the scope is empty, the precheck fails, the total is zero, or a demo is not yet matched. Clicking it creates the run and moves the user to the run's address.
sections.why: Stops users from starting a run that would have no projects to work from.
sections.watch_out: The start button depends on several conditions at once. Removing one of them would allow a run with no projects, which costs real resources.

sections.name: LessonsLearntPage (part 3)
sections.title: Recent runs and page layout
sections.what: Shows a list of saved runs with their status and creation time, or a loading, error or empty message. The layout also changes the page height depending on whether a run is open.
sections.why: Lets users reopen finished decks without starting over. The layout change lets a run view use the full screen height.
sections.watch_out: The saved run list is hidden in demo mode, so demo users cannot reopen their own runs from this screen.

sections.name: tool
sections.title: Tool registration details
sections.what: Describes this tool for the app: its short name, subtitle, status shown as LIVE, icon, web address and the page component. The app uses this to show the tool in menus and links.
sections.why: The app needs a standard description for every tool so it can list them and route to them.
sections.watch_out: The path here must match the path used in the links and the demo address on this page, or links will break.

summary: This is the main Lessons Learnt page: it lets a user pick a scope, starts a lessons run, and shows either the live run, a saved run, or the recorded demo.
purpose: Gives users one screen to choose projects or industries, see how many projects match, start a run that builds a lessons deck, and reopen past runs.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The file is split so the page decides what to show from the web address (run id, demo flag, replay flag) and hands the run display to other components.
how: The page reads the web address for a run id and demo flags. With no run open, it shows the scope picker, a precheck count, a start button, and a list of recent runs. With a run open, it hands off to RunSwitch, which loads the run every 2 seconds until it reaches a final status, then shows the matching view for its engine. Demo and replay modes use their own helpers.
inputs: The web address query values run, demo and replay; the user's choices in the scope picker; server data for runs, precheck results and industry names.
outputs: A full page with a scope summary, a start button, a list of saved runs, or a run view. Starting a run changes the web address to include the new run id.
risks: Starting a run is a real action that creates server work. The start button is disabled in several cases, but the code only checks the button state, so changing the page could make a second request possible. Polling every 2 seconds keeps requests going until a final status is seen.
debug: If the start button stays disabled, check the scope, the precheck result and the project total in the summary. If a run never finishes, check the status field from the run endpoint and whether the status is in the final list in llApi. If runs do not load, check the recent runs request and its error text.
